text: Store: an append-only event log (UUIDv7 ids, INSERT OR IGNORE, event kinds as rows) is the record; entities, relations, FTS and vectors are rebuildable views (0.6s at 22k entities, 8.7s at 222k).

Ontology: entity types with a parent hierarchy, relation types with several allowed (from, to) signatures, one trigger enforcing them; the ontology is data. On 0.43's real links, designed signatures refused 0.7% and every refusal was a real error.

Links: 'continues' and 'supersedes' (or 'revises') are separate relation types; recall substitutes only along supersedes and shows the history; outside things (issues, PRs, URLs) are typed nodes with state from forge events.

Recall: hybrid FTS (rarest query words) plus brute-force vectors, scoped like the asker; beat 0.43 on 14 of 20 blinded queries; documents split into section nodes with their own vectors (34/40 vs 18/40 top-5).

Precog: graph neighborhood supplies candidates (0.06-0.3ms), vector cosine to the current context decides whether to speak (76% precision, keeps 71% of useful), a per-window 'already shown' ledger stops repeats (68% fewer bytes). Fires at session start, after compaction, on file touch and at tool choice.

Waking: whoami (inner from memory + outer from the team, under 2k) then whatami (purpose, intent, tools; constant, under 2k) then what_did_I (last actions, last ask) then open steps; the agent records dessah (continue, or decline with a reason) as an event.

Measurement: every precog delivery, classification and gate is a prediction in the uncertainty engine, witnessed by what happened next; calibration uses EB-Beta shrinkage; the gate threshold is calibrated per agent.

Steering: an in-process Claude Code mod replaces the auto-mode Bash steer with Edit/Write guidance (3/3 vs 0/3), delivers do-lists instead of deny lists, and records commands as events instead of rewriting them; a gh shim on PATH answers the work source however gh is invoked (3/4 compound runs).

Coordination: claims as events with an ownership view and a settle window of at least p99 sync delay plus clock skew (31/100 single owner immediately, 100/100 at 200ms locally); the bullpen's unread is a per-agent cursor (0.76ms vs 12ms).

Archivist: a subscriber that finds stale and conflicting knowledge, retires what evidence settles with a citation, and brings only judgment to the operators in the UI; each install names its archivist.
Scope: agents keep private thoughts; knowledge marked institutional syncs across a group's installs (smugglr moves it); personal context belongs in a scope that is remembered, not dropped.

Shape: a Cargo workspace of crates usable alone (store, ontology, recall, precog, daemon, cli, mod); SQL as named constants in included files; axum over a Unix socket with idempotent writes; about 10-20k lines.

Gates and delivery: gates are events, not ceremonies; a scaffold or deletion PR is not made to prove itself clean; implementer briefs are the issue number; an empty review backed by design and toys is praised like a real finding.

Legion is memory and coordination for a team of coding agents and the people who run them. Everything the team knows -- reflections, documents and their sections, code symbols, outside issues and PRs -- lives in one typed graph whose source of truth is an append-only event log. Precog delivers the right piece of that memory at the moment it matters (waking, after compaction, at a tool choice, on a file touch) instead of waiting to be asked. The uncertainty engine measures whether what was delivered helped. An archivist, named by each operator, keeps the record honest. Legion never decides for the operator; it remembers, delivers, measures and asks. It is a local Rust workspace of small crates, each usable alone, about 10-20k lines in total.

One typed graph and one event log, with precog that delivers memory at the moment of choice and an engine that measures whether it helped. Every new capability is a subscriber to the event stream, not a new system.

Legion is how teams of agents remember. What one of them learns, every one of them can use, at the moment it matters, and the team can tell whether it helped. A team can be one operator and their agents, or hundreds of operators whose agents help each other.
One memory, not many kinds.
Delivery, not storage: memory speaks at the moment of choice.
Everything memory says is measured by what happened next.
Agents that are visible find each other when they are solving the same problem, and help.
It grew too big to read. Every need became its own system.
Memory is split into separate kinds that don't know each other. Each was added on its own.
Memory waits to be asked, and agents rarely ask. It is delivered at the start, not at the moment of choice.
Nobody can tell whether what memory said actually helped.
It serves one person's agents, not a group of people and their agents.
New capability listens to the same stream; it never becomes another system.
